title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Daily Interest Accrual and Cycle-End Crediting
content:
Interest on every Savings & Money Market Accounts product builds up one calendar day at a time and is paid when the statement cycle closes. This calculation guide defines each daily amount, how the components stack, how totals are rounded, and what happens at closure or when a past credit proves short.

## Rule

**The daily base.** Interest accrues on the balance at the end of each calendar day of the cycle, taking into account every ledger entry posted on or before that day.

**The earning threshold.** On a day whose end-of-day balance is below the tier's smallest earning balance, nothing accrues, in any component.

**Base rate from the ladder.** Where the tier uses the tiered method, one rate covers the entire balance, namely that of the top floor the balance has climbed to. Where the tier uses the blended method, the balance is divided at the floors and every slice sitting between two neighbouring floors is rated at its own band's yield.

**Daily amount.** A day's interest on a portion of balance is that portion multiplied by the annual percentage yield, divided by 100, and divided by **365**.

**Rounding.** Daily amounts are added up without rounding, separately for each component, and only each component's cycle total is rounded, half-up, to the cent.

**How components stack.** On the promotional share of a day's balance, the promotional rate stands in place of the base rate and neither the relationship bonus nor the goal bonus is added. The rest of that day's balance is rated at the base yield, lifted by the percentage points of the relationship bonus and of the goal bonus wherever each of them applies.

**Crediting.** On the cycle closing date each component is credited as its own interest entry, provided its rounded total is above 0.00. A component that does not apply to the account is treated as not applicable, not as a zero rate, and produces no entry.

**Rates in force.** Each day uses the tier and ladder that were in force on that day.

**Closing mid-cycle.** Interest accrued after the most recent cycle close is paid on closure only on a tier that pays accrued interest on closure; on any other tier it is forfeited.

**Correcting a short credit.** When a past cycle's interest was credited short, the correction is a separate interest entry, marked as a bank error, for the same cycle and component, and it pays the shortfall only.

## Worked example (hypothetical rates and balance)

Assume a tier paying a flat 0.50% under the tiered method, and a balance of 20000.00 held at every day's end through a 30-day cycle.

- One day's base interest: 20000.00 multiplied by 0.50, divided by 100, divided by 365, which is 0.27397260… unrounded.
- Thirty such days: 8.21917808… unrounded.
- Rounded half-up to the cent: 8.22 is credited as the base component.

Now assume instead that 5000.00 of the same balance were a promotional share at an assumed 3.00%. For each day, 5000.00 accrues at 3.00% only, and the other 15000.00 accrues at 0.50% plus any bonus points; the promotional component and the base component are summed and rounded separately.

## Points of judgement

**Is each day rounded to the cent?** No. Rounding happens once per component, on the cycle total.

**A cycle earned a relationship bonus that rounds to 0.00. Is a zero entry posted?** No. Only components above 0.00 after rounding are credited.
